{{Quote|Another complete failure. While the subject's base genetic code remains intact, the physical expressions have been&hellip;unsettling.|Lead Cloning Technician|<ref name="TFUIIvg" />}}
'''Aberrant clones''' were [[Blood/Legends|genetically]] flawed [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] of [[Galen Marek]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force user]] who served as the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|secret apprentice]] to the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] until his [[Light side of the Force/Legends|redemption]] and [[Death/Legends|death]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]. In seeking to [[Rule of Two/Legends|overthrow]] his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]], [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], Vader sought to create a new apprentice by using Marek's dead body as a [[Clone template/Legends|template]] for a clone who possessed all of Marek's skills, none of his emotional attachments, and was fully committed to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].

Utilizing an experimental version of the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] cloning process, Vader's [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] duplicated Marek's [[DNA/Legends|genetic code]] but encountered numerous setbacks as a result of attempting to replicate a [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-sensitive template. The initial test subjects were physically deformed and driven [[Clone madness|insane]] by the [[Memory flash|inherent memories]] of their progenitor. The procedure was gradually improved by the [[Lead Cloning Technician]], who succeeded in creating a new batch of clones that physically resembled Marek at the [[Time/Legends|time]] of his death. Nevertheless, they too suffered from an identity crisis due to the memory flashes that were meant to aid in their [[Sith training|training]]. Ultimately, the aberrant clones were kept in [[Suspended animation/Legends|stasis]] within the cloning facility of [[Timira City]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. Vader personally oversaw the training of clones who showed potential, casting aside each failure in an effort to find the one who met his expectations.

In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Assault on Kamino|attacked]] the Timira [[City/Legends|City]] cloning facility with the help of "[[Subject 1138|Starkiller]]," a renegade clone who [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|fled from Kamino]] after Vader deemed him another setback in a long line of failures. The rogue encountered multiple aberrant clones while attempting to rescue [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]] from Vader. Although Starkiller defeated the clones who attacked him, he regarded the manner of their deaths as a form of fratricide given that they were all created from the same source. He also recognized the mental instability of his clone brethren, having experienced his own sense of identity crisis due to the memories he possessed of another man's life.

==History==
===Origin===
{{Quote|We are still left with hundreds upon hundreds of abject failures. While they no longer try to kill anything that comes near them, they are nearly insensible.|Lead Cloning Technician, Timira City Cloning Facility|<ref name="TFUIIvg" />}}
[[File:Starkiller_clones.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Vader's initial efforts to clone the original Starkiller resulted in multiple aberrant failures.]]
The aberrant [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] came into existence as a result of clandestine project to replicate the [[Death/Legends|late]] [[Galen Marek]], the former [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. Shortly after Marek [[Battle on Death Star I|sacrificed]] his own life in defense of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] founders&mdash;[[Senator/Legends|senators]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]], [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]]&mdash;Vader transported the apprentice's body to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], intending to preserve the corpse as a [[Clone template/Legends|template]] from which the required [[DNA/Legends|DNA]] samples for cloning would be harvested.<ref name="TFUIIvg" />

Many obstacles hindered the project's success rate, however. First, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord's]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] resorted to using the accelerated cloning process, an experimental procedure that produced full-grown subjects in under a few weeks; the drawback being that all clones bred through this process would inevitably succumb to [[Clone madness|madness]] due to their rushed growth cycle.<ref name="TFUIIc">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (graphic novel)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' graphic novel]]</ref> Another dilemma that confounded the cloning technicians was [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] itself. By then, it had long been believed that clones could not be successfully created from [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] templates.<ref name="TFUIIvg" /><ref name="SWDP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> There was no definitive explanation for this phenomenon, but [[Ni-Ke-Vanz]] theorized that the Force inherently hindered the cloning process.<ref name="TFUIIn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> The third and most problematic obstacle was memory. In order for the new apprentice to utilize his inherent [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] and [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat skills]], Marek's memories would have to be [[Memory flash|imprinted]] on his replacement's own brain, thus transferring his knowledge and experience to his clone.<ref name="TFUIIvg" /> But through this, the clone would also develop an identity crisis as a result of possessing the memories and emotions of another person.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

Despite these obstacles, Darth Vader proceeded with his plans and the initial results produced a batch of hundreds of aberrant clones, all physically deformed and mentally unstable, and none of whom were considered successful by Vader's standards or his [[Lead Cloning Technician|lead cloning technician]].<ref name="TFUIIvg-db" /> The aberrant clones were put into [[Suspended animation/Legends|suspended animation]] within their [[cloning tank]]s;<ref name="TFUIIvg" /> the mistakes in their design would be gradually corrected, resulting in less flawed clones.<ref name="TFUIIvg-db" /> Meanwhile, Vader personally [[Sith training|trained]] several promising test subjects in the hopes that at least one clone would prove sufficient enough to become his new apprentice.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

===Fratricide===
[[File:Dark_Spirit_TFU2.png|thumb|250px|The renegade clone Starkiller saw several other clones of the same genetic source while experiencing a Force vision on Dagobah.]]
After [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of failed attempts, the project was finally deemed a success when a [[Dark Apprentice|single clone]] succeeded where all of his predecessors failed&mdash;he overcame the memory imprints of Galen Marek.<ref name="DT">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'': "Distant Thunder" cutscenes</ref> By compartmentalizing and isolating Marek's memories, he was able to differentiate his progenitor's thoughts from his own.<ref name="TFUIIvg-db" /> Around the same time, [[Subject 1138|another clone]] had nearly succeeded in his own trials, only to disappoint Vader when he failed to overcome his ingrained attachment to [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]],<ref name="TFUIIn" /> a trait that his successful counterpart also inherited but later suppressed.<ref name="DT" /> Realizing that he would be disposed of as a failed test subject, the renegade clone managed to [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escape from Kamino]], but later returned at the head of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Fleet]] in order to rescue Captain Eclipse.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

Just as the fighting began, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]&mdash;a cloned [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] hired by Darth Vader&mdash;encountered a lone aberrant clone who was armed with a [[red]]-bladed [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Driven by a sense of mindless rage, the clone attacked and nearly killed Fett, only to be killed when Fett desperately launched a [[Missile/Legends|missile]] from his [[Z-6 jetpack/Legends|Z-6 jetpack]] at the clone.<ref name="TFUIIc" />

During the fighting, the renegade clone&mdash;by then referred to as "Starkiller," the former codename of his template&mdash;infiltrated [[Timira City]] where he was confronted by Darth Vader and the aberrant clones. Until this point, Starkiller did not believe that there had been other clones before him. The sight of his "brothers," however imperfect, forced him to confront what he had believed from the start&mdash;he was a clone and the original Starkiller had perished, just as Vader had told him. In the aberrant clones, the only emotions he [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] were hate, rage and an overwhelming desire to kill. Yet they also exhibited confusion; they were all equally confused over their own identities.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

[[File:Starkiller-Walls.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The aberrant clones were destroyed by Starkiller, another clone of the late Galen Marek, during the assault on Kamino.]]
While defending himself against the clones, Starkiller took time to study his precursors. He noted that the first wave to attack him were the weakest and easiest to kill; the second group was cautious enough to keep their distance from their target who was armed with [[Starkiller's lightsabers|dual lightsabers]]. The last waves included clones who wielded [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], and those armed and trained in lightsaber combat. Despite the fact that they too possessed Marek's Force sensitivity, none of them could defeat the renegade clone in open battle. The ones who rushed at him were cut down, others were overpowered by his own command of the Force, and the rest attacked each other due to their unstable minds.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

As the [[Assault on Kamino]] concluded with a decisive Rebel victory, Starkiller successfully rescued Juno Eclipse and defeated Darth Vader, who was then taken into Alliance custody. In spite of his success, Starkiller remained conflicted over his ordeal with the aberrant clones. Aside from their differences with him and each other, as clones they all possessed the same attributes as Galen Marek in greater or lesser degrees. As such, Starkiller came to struggle with his own guilt for killing the aberrant clones, an action which he considered to be a form of fratricide&mdash;even suicide, since they were all genetic copies of the same man.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

==Powers and abilities==
[[File:StarkillerCloneSaberConceptArt-CEDAB.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Some of the aberrant clones were trained to wield two lightsabers, just like Starkiller and the Dark Apprentice.]]
Despite their many genetic flaws, the aberrant clones possessed Galen Marek's powerful affinity to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="TFUIIvg-db" /> But due to the psychological damage that they suffered in the cloning process, the clones would never be able to utilize Marek's abilities in a concentrated and focused way of combat. Since they were the first and most flawed versions of the clones, the genetically-inherited abilities of the original Starkiller were not evenly distributed among the aberrant clones.<ref name="TFUIIvg" />

Some clones were more skilled at using [[Force power/Legends|Force attacks]] such as [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] and [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force push]]. Other clones were equipped with dual [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] and specialized in the [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|fighting style]]. All of the aberrant clones, however, were capable of shielding themselves from basic Force attacks, except for [[Mind trick/Legends|Mind Control]].<ref name="TFUIIvg" /> Even so, they were helpless against the full power of a [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force Repulse]] when used by the [[Subject 1138|renegade clone]], as shown by how they were rendered into a fine bloody mist.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

==Behind the scenes==
In the Xbox/PC/PS3 versions of the game, the aberrant clones' [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] have silver [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]]. In the Wii version, they are colored red, purple, or orange. The colors indicate which technique they use, with the red lightsaber clones specializing in melee, purple ones using Force Lightning, and the orange ones using Force Push, as evidenced by how they break out of their tanks to attack Starkiller by the sound of Force Repulse.
